run.question:
Alertmanager alert RequestErrorRate (severity warning) is firing for service otel-demo/frontend-proxy since 2026-11-17T21:53:46Z.
Investigate why this alert is firing.

report.summary: The alert's non-zero request-error rate on otel-demo/frontend-proxy is real and is produced by frontend-proxy's own spans (143.20 ERROR ingress spans and 94.45 ERROR 'router frontend egress' spans over the 81-minute window) and by 5xx responses in its access log. The failing responses are attributed by the proxy to its upstream (`via_upstream`, `UC upstream_reset_before_response_started{connection_termination}`, `UT response_timeout`), and the frontend's own spans carry the matching errors (POST /api/cart, GET /api/cart, POST /api/checkout, grpc CartService/AddItem, CartService/GetCart, CheckoutService/PlaceOrder, tcp.connect). Two error periods are visible: an early one lasting to about 21:42-21:54 (15 s 504 timeouts on GET /api/data plus sporadic 503 upstream resets), and a larger burst at 21:56:38-22:02 that starts ~20 s after the cart Deployment was rolled out at 21:56:16 (new ReplicaSet cart-84889c965d, pod template annotation kubectl.kubernetes.io/restartedAt=2026-11-17T21:56:16Z, identical image and env to the old ReplicaSet cart-755465879b). The only fault-injection setting that is switched on in the namespace is cartFailure="on" ("Fail cart service") in ConfigMap flagd-config; every other flag there is "off". Against that, the cart service's own spans show no ERROR status, its pod logs contain no error lines and it served requests normally during the burst, so the declared cart fault itself was not directly observed, and the pre-21:56 timeouts/resets are not explained by cart. The cart Deployment restart is a mechanism, and ConfigMap flagd-config is the best-supported object-level cause; the conclusion is therefore partial.

claims.text: frontend-proxy's own spans record ERROR status in this window: span_name=ingress STATUS_CODE_ERROR increase 143.203125 against 22299.876923 STATUS_CODE_UNSET, and span_name='router frontend egress' STATUS_CODE_ERROR increase 94.453125 against 22352.890625 UNSET (81m window, 20:53:46-22:14:59Z).

frontend's own spans carry the corresponding errors over the same 81m: GET 23.370967, POST 71.129032, POST /api/cart 52.838709, GET /api/cart 23.370967, POST /api/checkout 18.290322, executing api route /api/cart 76.229508, grpc.oteldemo.CartService/AddItem 52.852459, grpc.oteldemo.CartService/GetCart 23.377049, grpc.oteldemo.CheckoutService/PlaceOrder 18.295081, tcp.connect 7.114754.

frontend's error rate (5m) is zero for GET /api/cart, POST /api/cart, POST /api/checkout, grpc CartService/AddItem, CartService/GetCart, CheckoutService/PlaceOrder and tcp.connect at every sampled step except the 21:58:46-22:00:46 steps, where it is 0.085-0.193; frontend-proxy ingress error rate is 0.172 at 21:34:46, falls to ~0.007-0.02 through 21:55, peaks at 0.351-0.363 at 21:58-22:02, then returns to ~0.012-0.015, and the 'router frontend egress' error rate is 0 outside 21:58-22:02 (0.344).

5m error ratio by service peaks at frontend-proxy 0.0279 and frontend 0.0256 in the 21:58 bucket; ad (0.0032), fraud-detection (0.0051) and recommendation (0.0017) show only small pre-existing ratios, and cart, checkout, payment, accounting report 0 in the sampled buckets.

frontend-proxy access log lines 21:56:38-21:56:52 show 500 responses coded by_upstream with a 21-byte body for GET /api/cart, POST /api/cart and POST /api/checkout, and lines at 21:57:33, 21:57:34, 21:58:39, 22:00:52 and 22:03:21 show '503 UC upstream_reset_before_response_started{connection_termination}' for GET /api/products/*, GET /api/recommendations and GET /api/cart.

The same frontend-proxy log holds earlier 5xx: '504 UT response_timeout' with 15001 ms durations on GET /api/data at 21:34:05-21:34:22, and isolated 503 UC upstream_reset_before_response_started{connection_termination} lines from 21:34:48 to 21:54:33 - i.e. non-zero frontend-proxy errors already before the alert's 21:53:46 start time.

Deployment cart was rolled out at 21:56:16 with an otherwise unchanged pod template: new ReplicaSet cart-84889c965d carries the annotation kubectl.kubernetes.io/restartedAt=2026-11-17T21:56:16Z and is 1/1 ready, old ReplicaSet cart-755465879b is scaled to 0, and both templates use the identical image ghcr.io/open-telemetry/demo:2.1.3-cart with identical env (FLAGD_HOST=flagd, VALKEY_ADDR=valkey-cart:6379, OTEL_RESOURCE_ATTRIBUTES service.name/version=2.1.3); Deployment cart shows generation 2 with 1 ready/available replica.

Events for that rollout: Deployment cart ScalingReplicaSet 'Scaled up replica set cart-84889c965d from 0 to 1' at 21:56:16, ReplicaSet cart-84889c965d SuccessfulCreate 'Created pod: cart-84889c965d-tkxdz', then ReplicaSet cart-755465879b SuccessfulDelete 'Deleted pod: cart-755465879b-rh5r4' with Pod cart-755465879b-rh5r4 Killing 'Stopping container cart' at 21:56:19 and Deployment cart 'Scaled down replica set cart-755465879b from 1 to 0' at 21:56:19.

ConfigMap flagd-config in namespace otel-demo holds switched-on fault-injection settings for exactly one service: cartFailure defaultVariant "on" (state ENABLED, description "Fail cart service", variants off=false/on=true). All other flags in the same ConfigMap are "off": adFailure, adHighCpu, adManualGc, emailMemoryLeak (0), imageSlowLoad (0), kafkaQueueProblems (0), loadGeneratorFloodHomepage (0), paymentFailure (0), paymentUnreachable, productCatalogFailure, recommendationCacheFailure.

otlp span metrics show cart spans with no ERROR status at all in the window: EXPIRE 4731.92, HGET 10020.19, HMSET 4730.31, POST 1172.65, POST /oteldemo.CartService/AddItem 3556.60, POST /oteldemo.CartService/GetCart 6461.07, POST /oteldemo.CartService/EmptyCart 1171.65, ResolveBoolean 1171.65 are all STATUS_CODE_UNSET; only the flagd EventStream span has an ERROR series and its increase is 0.

cart pod cart-84889c965d-tkxdz logs: a filter for err|exception|fail|panic|unavailable|refused over 3382 lines read for 21:50-22:10 matched exactly one benign startup line ('Overriding HTTP_PORTS ...'), and the unfiltered window 21:56:15-21:58:30 shows normal GetCartAsync/AddItemAsync/EmptyCartAsync calls from 21:58:22 onward.

All 21 otel-demo pods were Running at 22:15; cart-84889c965d-tkxdz had ready=true and restartCount 0 and startTime 2026-11-17T21:56:16Z, while fraud-detection-9fb7d885b-v48vh shows restartCount 1 with its 'Started container fraud-detection' event lastTimestamp 22:01:47Z (firstTimestamp 21:26:53).

checkout shows no error evidence of its own: its only error series in the window is oteldemo.CheckoutService/PlaceOrder with increase 0 and oteldemo.CartService/GetCart with increase 0, and its 5m error ratio is 0 in the sampled buckets, while its container was Ready in pod checkout-5dccddf8bb-cph2g.

All otel-demo Services exist with consistent selectors at query time, including cart (port 8080, selector opentelemetry.io/name=cart, clusterIP 100.64.112.47), checkout (100.65.226.162), frontend (100.65.91.250) and frontend-proxy (100.64.181.204).

frontend-proxy being the origin is rejected: the overwhelming majority of its spans are STATUS_CODE_UNSET (22299.88 of ~22443 ingress spans) and its failing responses are labelled via_upstream/UC/UT, i.e. the failure is attributed by the proxy to its upstream frontend, whose own spans carry matching ERROR status.

checkout, payment or the ad/fraud-detection/recommendation flagd EventStream errors as the cause of the burst is rejected: those services' error ratios are 0 or <=0.005 (flagd EventStream spans) and did not rise in the 21:58 bucket, whereas frontend and frontend-proxy rose to 0.0256 and 0.0279.

The switched-on setting cartFailure="on" in ConfigMap flagd-config (namespace otel-demo) is the best-supported object-level cause of the observed failure: it is the only enabled fault flag, it names the cart service, the cart Deployment was restarted at 21:56:16 with an otherwise unchanged pod template, and the frontend's cart/checkout 5xx (500s in the frontend-proxy log and ERROR grpc CartService/AddItem, GetCart, CheckoutService/PlaceOrder and tcp.connect spans) begin ~20 s after that restart. The restart is the mechanism; the ConfigMap is where the fault is declared.

The declared cart fault was not observed on cart itself: cart spans show no ERROR status (all UNSET), cart pod logs over 21:50-22:10 contain no error/exception/fail lines, and cart served GetCartAsync/AddItemAsync normally at 21:58 and 22:06 - so the cartFailure fault taking effect is inferred, not seen.

Not all observed errors fit the cart hypothesis: frontend-proxy was already producing errors before the 21:56:16 cart restart - 504 UT response_timeout of 15001 ms on GET /api/data at 21:34:05-21:34:22 and isolated 503 UC resets from 21:34:48 to 21:54:33 on /api/products, /api/recommendations, /api/data and /api/cart - and a low error ratio persists after the burst (0.0003-0.0007 in the last 5m buckets). Those endpoints do not all involve cart.

gaps: The alert's own definition is unavailable: list_prometheus_rules with rule_name=RequestErrorRate returned nothing (no_data), so the exact expression and window behind the reported 0.01111111111111111 cannot be verified against the metric series.

No trace-level error detail exists for the burst: Jaeger's newest returned traces for frontend end at 21:42:12, and traces_search for frontend-proxy (21:58-22:02) and frontend (21:59-22:00) returned nothing, so the gRPC status codes/messages of the failing cart and checkout calls are unknown.

It cannot be determined when ConfigMap flagd-config's cartFailure was switched from off to on: the change_history integration is not available in this Run, and the flagd pod's containers produced no readable log lines (0 bytes, flagd-77f6d5b95d-64j8j).

The cart service's side of the failure is not directly observed: cart spans are all STATUS_CODE_UNSET and its logs show no exceptions, so whether cart returned FailedPrecondition (the declared fault) or the frontend merely lost its connections is unresolved.
The frontend container produced no readable log lines for 21:54-22:05 (0 bytes), so frontend-side exception text for the 500s and connection resets is unknown.

The earlier 504 UT response_timeout burst on GET /api/data at 21:34 and the sporadic 503 UC upstream resets between 21:34:48 and 21:54:33 remain unexplained; no declared fault setting other than cartFailure is enabled, and no dependency showed errors of its own in that period.

checkout's error path is unconfirmed: a log query for err|fail|exception|refused|unavailable|deadline on pod checkout-5dccddf8bb-cph2g for 21:55-21:58:30 returned nothing, which is only an empty query result and not proof that no error occurred.
next_steps: Obtain the Prometheus rule definition of RequestErrorRate (expression, window, for-duration) to confirm which signal the alert tracks.

Check change/audit history of ConfigMap flagd-config (otel-demo/demo.flagd.json) and of the kubectl rollout restart that set kubectl.kubernetes.io/restartedAt=2026-11-17T21:56:16Z on Deployment cart, to establish who switched cartFailure to on and when.
Capture frontend application logs or enable its error logging to record the gRPC status of failed cart/checkout calls during a recurrence.

Review the pre-existing 15 s timeouts on GET /api/data and the sporadic 503 upstream_reset events separately, since they predate the cart restart and are not explained by the enabled cartFailure flag.

data.relay:
connectors:
  spanmetrics:
    dimensions:
    - default: otel-demo
      name: namespace
exporters:
  clickhouse:
    endpoint: http://clickhouse-clickhouse.clickhouse.svc.cluster.local:8123
    logs_table_name: otel_demo_logs
    password: ""
    traces_table_name: otel_demo_traces
    username: default
  debug: {}
  opensearch:
    http:
      endpoint: http://opensearch-master.opensearch.svc.cluster.local:9200
      tls:
        insecure: true
    logs_index: otel-logs
    logs_index_time_format: yyyy-MM-dd
  otlp:
    endpoint: jaeger-collector.opentelemetry-collectors.svc.cluster.local:4317
    tls:
      insecure: true
  otlphttp/prometheus:
    endpoint: http://prometheus-kube-prometheus-prometheus.prometheus.svc.cluster.local:9090
    tls:
      insecure: true
  prometheus:
    endpoint: 0.0.0.0:8889
extensions:
  health_check:
    endpoint: ${env:MY_POD_IP}:13133
processors:
  batch: {}
  k8sattributes:
    extract:
      metadata:
      - k8s.namespace.name
      - k8s.deployment.name
      - k8s.statefulset.name
      - k8s.daemonset.name
      - k8s.cronjob.name
      - k8s.job.name
      - k8s.node.name
      - k8s.pod.name
      - k8s.pod.uid
      - k8s.pod.start_time
    passthrough: false
    pod_association:
    - sources:
      - from: resource_attribute
        name: k8s.pod.ip
    - sources:
      - from: resource_attribute
        name: k8s.pod.uid
    - sources:
      - from: connection
  memory_limiter:
    check_interval: 5s
    limit_percentage: 80
    spike_limit_percentage: 25
  resource:
    attributes:
    - action: insert
      from_attribute: k8s.pod.uid
      key: service.instance.id
  resourcedetection:
    detectors:
    - env
    - system
  transform:
    error_mode: ignore
    trace_statements:
    - context: span
      statements:
      - replace_pattern(name, "\\?.*", "")
      - replace_match(name, "GET /api/products/*", "GET /api/products/{productId}")
receivers:
  httpcheck/frontend-proxy:
    targets:
    - endpoint: http://frontend-proxy:8080
  jaeger:
    protocols:
      grpc:
        endpoint: ${env:MY_POD_IP}:14250
      thrift_compact:
        endpoint: ${env:MY_POD_IP}:6831
      thrift_http:
        endpoint: ${env:MY_POD_IP}:14268
  nginx:
    collection_interval: 10s
    endpoint: http://image-provider:8081/status
  otlp:
    protocols:
      grpc:
        endpoint: ${env:MY_POD_IP}:4317
      http:
        cors:
          allowed_origins:
          - http://*
          - https://*
        endpoint: ${env:MY_POD_IP}:4318
  postgresql:
    endpoint: postgresql:5432
    metrics:
      postgresql.blks_hit:
        enabled: true
      postgresql.blks_read:
        enabled: true
      postgresql.deadlocks:
        enabled: true
      postgresql.tup_deleted:
        enabled: true
      postgresql.tup_fetched:
        enabled: true
      postgresql.tup_inserted:
        enabled: true
      postgresql.tup_returned:
        enabled: true
      postgresql.tup_updated:
        enabled: true
    password: [REDACTED_CREDENTIAL]
    tls:
      insecure: true
    username: root
  prometheus:
    config:
      scrape_configs:
      - job_name: opentelemetry-collector
        scrape_interval: 10s
        static_configs:
        - targets:
          - ${env:MY_POD_IP}:8888
  redis:
    collection_interval: 10s
    endpoint: valkey-cart:6379
    username: valkey
  zipkin:
    endpoint: ${env:MY_POD_IP}:9411
service:
  extensions:
  - health_check
  pipelines:
    logs:
      exporters:
      - clickhouse
      - debug
      processors:
      - k8sattributes
      - memory_limiter
      - resourcedetection
      - resource
      - batch
      receivers:
      - otlp
    metrics:
      exporters:
      - debug
      - prometheus
      processors:
      - k8sattributes
      - memory_limiter
      - resourcedetection
      - resource
      - batch
      receivers:
      - httpcheck/frontend-proxy
      - nginx
      - otlp
      - postgresql
      - redis
      - spanmetrics
    traces:
      exporters:
      - clickhouse
      - debug
      - otlp
      - spanmetrics
      processors:
      - k8sattributes
      - memory_limiter
      - resourcedetection
      - resource
      - transform
      - batch
      receivers:
      - otlp
      - jaeger
      - zipkin
  telemetry:
    metrics:
      level: detailed
      readers:
      - pull:
          exporter:
            prometheus:
              host: 0.0.0.0
              port: 8888

view.cannot_prove: Objects are the cluster's state when the query ran, not during the incident window: they cannot prove what was true earlier, and an object missing now may have existed then. Events cover only their own timestamps inside the window; an event that is not returned is unknown, not proof nothing happened (events expire and timestamps are often null). A jq result is what the expression selected, not a full picture of the kind.
